title: Triple plaque purification to generate clonal phage lysates
author: Melissa B Duhaime

steps.title: Perform First Plaque Purification
steps.instruction: Pick a representative plaque from an overnight agar overlay screening plate and bring it into solution.

substeps.instruction: Pick a plaque similar in morphology and size to the majority of others using a 200 ul pipette tip.
Mark the plate to indicate which plaque was picked.
Vortex the pipette tip in 1 mL of phage buffer.
Let the sample stand for at least 30 minutes.
Vortex again before plating.

steps.title: Plate and Incubate First Round
steps.instruction: Plate dilutions of the sample and incubate to obtain countable plaques.

substeps.instruction: Plate dilutions from 10^-2 to 10^-6.
Incubate overnight at room temperature (16-28 hours).

steps.title: Perform Second Plaque Purification
steps.instruction: Repeat the picking and plating process for a second round of purification.

substeps.instruction: Pick a plaque from the overnight plates.
Vortex the tip in 1 mL phage buffer, let stand for 30 minutes, and vortex again.
Plate dilutions (10^-2 to 10^-6) and incubate overnight at room temperature (16-28 hours).

steps.title: Perform Third Plaque Purification
steps.instruction: Repeat the picking and plating process for a third round of purification.

substeps.instruction: Pick a plaque from the second round plates.
Vortex the tip in 1 mL phage buffer, let stand for 30 minutes, and vortex again.
Plate dilutions (10^-2 to 10^-6) and incubate overnight at room temperature (16-28 hours).

steps.title: Prepare Clonal Phage Lysate
steps.instruction: Generate a high-titer lysate from the third purification round.

substeps.instruction: Pick a plaque from the Purification 3 plate using a 200 µl pipette tip.
Vortex the tip in 1 mL of phage buffer, let stand for at least 30 minutes, and vortex again.
Plate a dilution that will lyse 95% of the host lawn and incubate for 24 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Harvest Phage from Plate
steps.instruction: Extract phages from the lysed host lawn.

substeps.instruction: Identify plates that are 95% lysed (acceptable range is down to 70%; do not use completely lysed plates).
Hold the plate at an angle and gently pipette 5 mL of phage buffer onto the plate.
Place on a platform shaker at 70 rpm for 30 minutes to 3 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Clarify and Filter Lysate
steps.instruction: Collect and purify the phage suspension.

substeps.instruction: Use a serological pipette to extract the liquid into a 15 mL conical tube.
If solid matter is present, centrifuge the sample at 3220 g for 5 min and extract the supernatant.
Using a 5-10 mL syringe, filter the sample into a new 15 mL conical tube using a 0.8/0.2 um filter (blue and green).

steps.title: Titer and Concentrate Lysate
steps.instruction: Determine the phage concentration and concentrate if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Plate plaque assays on corresponding hosts at dilutions from 10^-1 to 10^-9.
Incubate plates for 24 hours and count plaques the following day.
If the titer is fewer than 3 x 10^9 phage/mL, make multiple plate lysates and concentrate the combined lysate using PEG or Amicon filtration cartridges.
